_comment: Generated: each operation's command-line command. go test ./internal/cli -run TestCommandIndex checks it; METARUSH_UPDATE_COMMANDS=1 rewrites it. Do not edit by hand.

ability.approve.help: Approve a version of an ability for the workspace, or turn it down — owners, at an interactive terminal: what it may do is shown first

ability.check.help: Check an ability's folder (or, with --version, a version brought in from another workspace): its manifest, no keys or oversized files, its test run once in the sandbox with the network off; a version that passes waits for an owner

ability.export.help: Export a version of an ability to a file another workspace can bring in (its approval here goes along as information only)

ability.find.help: Find abilities for a task: at most eight, one line each (what it does, whether it is set up here, its cost, what leaves)

ability.import.help: Bring in an ability file from another workspace as a draft: never approved or set up here; check it on this computer, then an owner approves it

ability.list.help: List the abilities: what each does, whether an owner approved it, whether it is set up here, its cost and what leaves this computer

ability.plan.help: Show what a run would do before anything runs: inputs, the estimate, places and keys, what leaves this computer, what it brings back, who decides

ability.revoke.help: Take an ability's approval back — owners, at an interactive terminal: nothing runs that version until an owner approves it again

ability.run.help: Run an approved ability on this computer: the plan is shown first; a person starts any run that costs money, sends pictures, sound or footage away, or changes something outside MetaRush

ability.runs.help: List runs of abilities, or show one with the requests it made through MetaRush and what it printed

ability.setup.usage: metarush ability setup <name> [--program name=/full/path] [--file name=/full/path] [--key name] [--agree-local] [--forget]
ability.setup.help: Set an ability up on this computer — a person, at an interactive terminal: the programs it runs, pinned by fingerprint, and its keys (owners; typed, never on the command line)

ability.show.help: Show an ability: what an owner approves it from (what it installs, places, keys, what leaves, cost, licence), its inputs, versions and runs

account.avatar.help: Set your picture from a PNG, JPEG or WebP file (kept as a small square), or remove it with --remove

account.password.help: Change your own password (asks for the current one); signs you out everywhere

account.preferences.help: Your preferences: estimate costs of outside AI services before edits (on by default), Ask first or Auto; owners can ask everyone for estimates

account.preferences.set.help: Your preferences: estimate costs of outside AI services before edits (on by default), Ask first or Auto; owners can ask everyone for estimates

account.signoutEverywhere.help: Sign yourself out on every computer and browser

account.update.help: Change your own name or email (an email change asks for your password)

activity.summary.help: What MetaRush is doing now: uploads, footage being prepared, renders, quality checks, Claude Code requests, and why anything is waiting

add.cloud.help: Bring files in from a Google Drive or Dropbox folder through your own rclone on this computer, without syncing it

add.cloud.list.help: Bring files in from a Google Drive or Dropbox folder through your own rclone on this computer, without syncing it

add.links.help: Add anything, the way the Add box does: footage to the project (or the Inbox), pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts to its resources, folders as linked folders, and links to the link import

add.paths.help: Add anything, the way the Add box does: footage to the project (or the Inbox), pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts to its resources, folders as linked folders, and links to the link import

add.route.help: Add anything, the way the Add box does: footage to the project (or the Inbox), pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts to its resources, folders as linked folders, and links to the link import

ai.cancel.help: Stop AI work that is waiting or being made

ai.estimate.help: Price AI work and check it may be made (the model, alternatives, consent, budget, this computer's key); nothing is sent or spent

ai.list.help: AI work with what it cost (pictures, speech, sound effects, music, dubs, transcripts, voice copies)

ai.local.help: The AI models that run on this computer — free, no key, nothing leaves it — and whether each is set up

ai.local.setup.help: Set up an AI model that runs on this computer: its pinned files are downloaded once and checked (people only)

ai.make.help: Make a picture, speech, a sound effect, music, a voice change, a dub or a cloud transcript: priced first, made with the price you agree to

ai.models.help: The models for each kind of AI work, with prices, licence and data terms, and what a project's Content Settings allow

ai.rules.help: Which AI services a project's work may go to (the AI services part of its Content Settings)

ai.rules.set.help: Choose which AI services the work of projects using these Content Settings may go to: none, never some providers, or a model per kind of work (people only)

ai.show.usage: metarush ai show <work, clip or picture>
ai.show.help: How a piece of AI work was made: the model and why, what was sent, licence and data terms, cost, consent and what it made

ai.voices.help: Voice copies: list them, copy a person's voice with their consent, withdraw one

ai.voices.copy.help: Copy a person's voice with their consent (and, where the service wants it, them reading its consent script) — people only, priced first

ai.voices.remove.help: Withdraw a voice copy: deleted at the provider, and nothing more is said with it (people only)

asset.archive.help: File clips in the Archive (“keep for later”): out of the Inbox without a project; with --project they leave that project too. Nothing is deleted

asset.card.help: A clip's or picture's info card: its name and original file, where it came from, what MetaRush found, where it's used, its fixes

asset.delete.help: Delete footage for good (the file, preview, transcript and speaker data, on every machine) — people only, in their own terminal; refused while any project but this one has it or any cut uses it

asset.duplicate.help: Decide about a file identical to a clip you already have: --keep keeps its name too (stored once), --skip changes nothing

asset.fixes.usage: metarush asset fixes <clip-or-picture> [--tick steady,colour] [--untick grain] [--only …|--none] [--kind camera|call|voice|music] [--again] [--look] [--wait]
asset.fixes.help: A source's fixes: what fits and why; tick or untick them (the original is kept; a fixed copy is made on a worker), or measure again

asset.fixes.look.usage: metarush asset fixes <clip-or-picture> [--tick steady,colour] [--untick grain] [--only …|--none] [--kind camera|call|voice|music] [--again] [--look] [--wait]
asset.fixes.look.help: A source's fixes: what fits and why; tick or untick them (the original is kept; a fixed copy is made on a worker), or measure again

asset.fixes.set.usage: metarush asset fixes <clip-or-picture> [--tick steady,colour] [--untick grain] [--only …|--none] [--kind camera|call|voice|music] [--again] [--look] [--wait]
asset.fixes.set.help: A source's fixes: what fits and why; tick or untick them (the original is kept; a fixed copy is made on a worker), or measure again

asset.link.help: Add a clip to a project (or take it out with --unlink: the footage stays in the workspace, in the Inbox when no project has it)

asset.list.help: List footage (a project's, the Inbox's or all of it)

asset.move.help: Move footage from one project (or, without --from, the Inbox) to another

asset.names.help: Better, descriptive names MetaRush suggests for clips (who is in them, what they're about); --accept-all uses them, keeping names people gave

asset.names.accept.help: Better, descriptive names MetaRush suggests for clips (who is in them, what they're about); --accept-all uses them, keeping names people gave

asset.precheck.help: Before adding: which files MetaRush already has, which repeat in the list, and which are new

asset.restore.help: Put clips in the Trash back where they were (their project, collections, the Archive; else the Inbox)

asset.rights.usage: metarush asset rights <asset-id> --license "<what allows using it>" [--source <url>] [--attribution "<credit>"]
asset.rights.help: Record where a music or audio file comes from and whether you may use it

asset.show.help: Show one clip: what it is, how far along it is, where it came from (--json has everything)

asset.trash.help: Move clips to the Trash (they can be restored; nothing is deleted until the Trash is emptied); refused while a project's latest cut uses one or another project has it

asset.unarchive.help: Take clips out of the Archive (back in the Inbox unless a project or collection has them)

asset.update.help: Rename a clip: a descriptive title (its original file name stays as file info), or MetaRush's suggested name with --suggested

asset.where.help: List every place footage is used: its projects, projects that see it through a link, and the cuts (and older versions) that play it

assistant.act.help: Do, answer or set aside what Claude asked for (one card, several, --all, or a question card); people only (you confirm in this terminal)

assistant.apply.help: Apply one of a conversation's plans (the confirm token comes from `assistant proposals`, like `edit apply`)

assistant.archive.help: Archive a conversation (--restore brings it back)

assistant.ask.help: Start a conversation with Claude Code (it reads and proposes; you apply)

assistant.attach.help: Start a conversation with Claude Code (it reads and proposes; you apply)

assistant.configure.help: Change a conversation's model, effort or limit (from its next message on, also after a resume)

assistant.continue.help: Send a follow-up message (queued while Claude is working); only on the machine that holds the conversation

assistant.dequeue.help: Remove a queued message before it is sent

assistant.interrupt.help: Interrupt Claude's current turn (the conversation goes on; queued messages are handed back)

assistant.list.help: List conversations, most recent first (a project's: everyone's; otherwise yours)

assistant.mode.help: Whether Claude's changes for you wait for your OK (ask, the default) or run by themselves when they can be undone (auto); choosing is people only

assistant.mode.set.help: Whether Claude's changes for you wait for your OK (ask, the default) or run by themselves when they can be undone (auto); choosing is people only

assistant.models.help: List the models and effort levels the installed Claude Code offers (no prompt is sent)

assistant.proposals.help: List a conversation's plans and render requests, checked against the current head (with confirm tokens)

assistant.settings.help: Show or change the installation defaults: model, effort, the per-conversation limit, summaries and the cache

assistant.settings.set.help: Show or change the installation defaults: model, effort, the per-conversation limit, summaries and the cache

assistant.show.help: Show a conversation: messages, Claude's replies, steps and proposals (--raw adds the exact prompts and tool I/O)

assistant.spending.help: When Auto spends money by itself: the budgets and daily limits a person set with each service, and what it spent for you today

assistant.status.help: Check whether Claude Code can run here (version, sign-in, billing mode, limits); no prompt is sent

assistant.stop.help: End the conversation's Claude Code process (a later message resumes the session)

assistant.suggestions.help: Suggest a few things to ask Claude for the current project or workspace

audit.list.help: Read the audit trail: who did what, from which machine and channel

auth.method.set.help: Choose how people sign in, giving your own sign-in at the same step (people only, on this computer)

auth.reset.help: Put sign-in back to a fresh install's: just you on this computer, everyone signed out, people kept with their history (people only)

auth.status.help: How people sign in here, and who you are

brand.apply.help: Use the brand in a project's latest cut — the brand of the settings it uses: its colours, font and logos (shows the change first)

brand.set.help: Change the brand of a project's own Content Settings, or without --project the default's (resources are named like everywhere; colours come from the logo unless you set them); --from-site takes what a website snapshot suggests, --apply also puts it on the project's latest cut

brand.show.help: Show the brand a project uses (from its Content Settings: its own, another project's or the default's) and the brand new cuts get

brand.suggest.help: Suggest a brand kit from a website snapshot: its logo, colours and font, each with why (nothing is saved; brand set --from-site takes it)

cache.prefetch.help: Download what a render or review needs (footage, preview copies, the latest render) so this machine works offline

cache.prune.help: Free space: remove what was used longest ago from this machine's copy (never what is kept for offline work or in use; MetaRush's storage keeps everything)

cache.repair.help: Check every file in this machine's copy, remove damaged ones and unfinished downloads, and download again what is kept for offline work

cache.status.help: How much this machine's copy uses, what is kept here for offline work, and how it is kept under its limit

captions.at.help: Which words the caption on screen at a moment of a version shows, where they are said, and what the transcript says there now

captions.check.help: Words in a version's captions worth a look before it goes out

captions.file.help: A version's captions as a file, with every text fix made since (no new render); --version-words: the words its video shows

captions.languages.help: The languages a project's captions are translated into, and how many of a version's lines each has

captions.lines.help: A version's caption lines to translate into a language, what is translated already, and the spelling list as the glossary

captions.looks.help: The caption looks a cut can use, what each looks like and suits (and the project's house style's)

captions.translate.help: Keep a translation of a version's caption lines (marked as machine-translated unless --human); delivery writes a captions file per language

captions.translation.remove.help: Take a language's translated captions off a project (delivered videos keep their files)

catalogue.list.help: List the abilities, built in and added, group by group, each saying whether it works here now or what it needs

catalogue.show.help: Show one ability: what it does, what it needs, whether it works here, and what runs it

collection.add.help: Put clips on a collection (they leave the Inbox and stay in their projects); --create makes the collection if there is none by that name

collection.delete.help: Delete a collection, never its clips (a clip on nothing else goes back to the Inbox; clips a project's cut uses through it join that project)

collection.list.help: List collections: how many clips each has and the projects that use it

collection.remove.help: Take clips off a collection (nothing is deleted; a clip on nothing else goes back to the Inbox)

collection.show.help: Show a collection: its clips (and where else each one is) and the projects that use it

components.add.help: Add an optional component to this computer (people only): with Homebrew where it is, else MetaRush's own checked download

components.list.help: What MetaRush can use on this computer: what each optional part unlocks, whether it is here, and adding or removing one

components.remove.help: Remove an optional component MetaRush added to this computer, and stop it being set up by itself (people only)

consent.list.help: Consent records and whether each is in force

consent.record.help: Record consent: your own statement (--self), or their recording (--recording) (people only)

consent.revoke.help: Withdraw a consent: nothing new is made with that likeness (people only)

consent.show.help: A consent record: who, the statement, what it covers, until when

content.follow.help: Make a project use another project's settings (live), or with --default the default's

content.gate.set.help: Owners: whether the videos of every project using a project's own settings wait for the quality check and sign-offs (on), only remind (off) or follow the workspace

content.leave.help: What of a project may leave this computer, and to whom: footage, voices, faces, words and pictures, to AI services, abilities, Claude, cloud storage, delivery and people outside the workspace

content.leave.set.usage: metarush content leave set [--project <project>] [--nothing|--anything] [--keep place=kinds] [--let place=kinds] [--only place=who] [--anyone place]
content.leave.set.help: Change what of the projects using a project's own Content Settings may leave this computer (people only; letting more leave takes an owner)

content.logo.remove.help: Take one of the brand's logos away (the picture stays in the resources; saved versions keep it)

content.logo.set.usage: metarush content logo set <main|dark|light|icon|wordmark> <file or resource> [--project <project>]
content.logo.set.help: Make a picture one of the brand's logos: a file on this computer (added to the resources first) or a resource's name

content.own.help: Give a project its own settings: empty (or the ones it had before), or with --copy a copy of what it uses now

content.pack.accept.help: Make the proposed layout pack the pack of a project's settings (people only, in a terminal or the dashboard)

content.pack.apply.help: Make a project's latest cut follow the layout pack of the settings it uses (shows the change first)

content.pack.decline.help: Set the proposed layout pack aside (the pack stays as it was)

content.pack.preview.help: Previews of the layout pack in the brand and house style (with --json: a plan per graphic the dashboard plays, and where call layouts place the pictures)

content.pack.propose.help: Propose a whole layout pack for a project's settings (its graphics may be project motion graphics): a draft a person accepts

content.pack.set.help: Change the layout pack of a project's own settings (without --project: the default's); settings without one start from MetaRush's own

content.pack.show.help: The layout pack of the settings a project uses (without --project: the default's), and a proposed pack waiting for a person

content.rules.add.help: Add a house rule to a project's own settings (without --project: the default's); every project using them follows it (--promise: a promise made to the client)

content.rules.list.help: The house rules of the settings a project uses (without --project: the default's)

content.rules.remove.help: Take a house rule out (its number, ID or words; taking back a promise is a person's)

content.setDefault.help: Use a project's settings for new projects (its "Use for new projects"; the one default moves here)

content.show.help: Whose Content Settings a project uses, what they hold and who else uses them (without --project: the default's)

content.signoffs.add.usage: metarush content signoffs add "<who OKs what>" [--project <project>]
content.signoffs.add.help: Add a house sign-off to a project's own settings (without --project: the default's); every project using them waits for it

content.signoffs.list.help: The house sign-offs of the settings a project uses (without --project: the default's)

content.signoffs.remove.help: Take a house sign-off out (its number, ID or words)

content.style.apply.help: Make a project's latest cut follow the house style of the settings it uses (shows the change first)

content.style.set.usage: metarush content style set [--project <project>] [--captions on|off] [--caption-look …] [--caption-size …] [--caption-position …] [--name-bar-look band|tab] [--name-bar-height full|half] [--name-bar-animates fade|slide|never] [--name-titles clean|cinematic] [--framing faces|follow|fixed] [--cut-blend <s>] [--level-speech on|off] [--intro title.card|slide.title|none …] [--end-card endcard.cta|slide.title|none …] [--clear <part>]
content.style.set.help: Change the house style of a project's own settings (without --project: the default's); an empty value goes back to MetaRush's own

content.style.show.help: The house style of the settings a project uses (without --project: the default's)

conversation.angle.help: Change what a conversation clip shows from a moment on: a person, a layout, a card or a cutaway

conversation.cleanup.help: Look for what calls leave behind: call talk, dead air, frozen webcams, sound dropouts, the app's labels

conversation.create.help: Make a conversation from several recordings of one talk, lined up by their sound

conversation.cut.help: Cut a conversation automatically in a style: whoever is talking, reactions, split layouts, each choice explained

conversation.decide.help: Accept or skip clean-up suggestions (accepting changes the cut: cut out, someone else shown, a crop)

conversation.detect.help: Say whether a folder (or a list of files) is a call recording, who is in it and which file is whose

conversation.import.help: Bring in a call app's recording folder (Zoom, Riverside, SquadCast, or one recording per person) as a conversation

conversation.list.help: The conversations, with their people, length and how sure their sync is

conversation.match.help: Match the webcams: brightness, contrast and colour fitted to one person's picture, measured before and after

conversation.moments.help: The best moments for shorts: complete stretches that start cleanly, and why each might work

conversation.nudge.help: Move one recording earlier or later on the conversation's clock (when lips and voice don't match)

conversation.pin.help: Use the conversation's current alignment and member settings in the project's cut

conversation.settings.help: How the cut plays a conversation: microphones quieter when their person isn't speaking, name tags, a person's crop

conversation.short.help: Make a short from a stretch: a new project with a vertical cut of its own (or the episode's stretch nested)

conversation.show.help: A conversation's recordings, how each lines up and how sure, and the cuts that play it

conversation.styles.help: The styles an automatic cut can have, and the layouts

conversation.sync.help: Line the recordings up again: by their sound, on a clap, on moments you mark, or as files that start together

conversation.update.help: Rename it, or change a member: name, name tag, what their recording gives, who they are in People

cut.add.help: Put footage into the cut as a new clip: all of it, or from a time (or words) to another

cut.apply.help: Save a checked cut sheet as a new revision (in a terminal, without --confirm, it asks you first)

cut.captions.usage: metarush cut captions <project> [--look <look>] [--size small|medium|large] [--position bottom|lower|middle|top] [--words-per-line N] [--on|--off] [--dry-run | --confirm <token>]
cut.captions.help: Choose how the cut's captions look: one of the vetted looks, their size and place, words per line, on or off

cut.check.help: Check a cut sheet: problems by line, the changes in plain words, and a confirm token

cut.compare.help: Compare two versions (--format md: the changes in plain words plus the cut sheet lines that differ)

cut.copyIn.usage: metarush cut copy-in <project> <other project> [--revision rN] [--after <clip> | --before <clip> | --at start|end|N]
cut.copyIn.help: Copy another project's cut into this cut as a starting point: clips, transitions, graphics, sound and narration (no live link)

cut.delete.help: Remove clips from the cut; the rest closes up

cut.deleteRange.help: Cut out a stretch of the video (times in the video, across clips); the rest closes up

cut.diff.help: Compare a cut sheet with the revision it came from and with the latest revision

cut.flashes.help: Trim the split-second flashes of another picture at the edges of the latest cut's clips, at the exact switch

cut.framing.help: Choose how crops are framed: follow the subject as it moves, keep faces in frame, or keep the middle (the whole cut, or one clip)

cut.move.usage: metarush cut move <project> <clip> <start | end | after <clip> | before <clip> | <place>>
cut.move.help: Move a clip to the start, the end, next to another clip or to a place number

cut.names.help: Cover the names a call app printed in the picture with your own name bar for the whole video

cut.nest.usage: metarush cut nest <project> <other project> [--revision rN] [--after <clip> | --before <clip> | --at start|end|N] [--in 0:02] [--out 0:10]
cut.nest.help: Put another project's cut into this cut as one clip, pinned to one version (picture, sound, narration and graphics as it plays there)

cut.pauses.help: Shorten long pauses between words anywhere in the cut, each one heard first

cut.removeWords.help: Take words out of the cut (cutting in the pauses around them), or ums, repeats and false starts

cut.rename.help: Name a project's cut descriptively (“Main open day video”), or take MetaRush's suggestion; no new version is saved and approvals stay

cut.say.estimate.help: Price changing words someone said into new words in their own voice copy, and check it may be made; nothing is sent or spent

cut.say.list.help: List words changed in a speaker's own voice copy: before and after, whose voice, how they were checked, whether the cut plays them

cut.say.make.help: Make new words in the speaker's own voice copy (people only, priced first); they're checked before they can go in the cut

cut.say.mouth.help: Match the mouth to checked new words (lip sync over the stretch, with everyone's consent): priced first, people only

cut.say.place.help: Put checked new words into the cut as a new version, with a review copy (people only)

cut.say.show.help: Show a word change made in a speaker's own voice copy: before and after, voice and consent, price, checks, versions

cut.say.undo.help: Take changed words out of the cut again: a new version plays what was said

cut.show.help: Print a revision as a cut sheet (default: the latest)

cut.signoffs.add.usage: metarush cut signoffs add <project> "<who OKs what>"
cut.signoffs.add.help: Add a sign-off (Lena OKs the final version)

cut.signoffs.done.help: Tick a sign-off: that OK was given

cut.signoffs.list.help: List the sign-offs a cut needs

cut.signoffs.remove.help: Take a sign-off off the checklist

cut.signoffs.undo.help: Untick a sign-off: the OK is needed again

cut.split.usage: metarush cut split <project> <time in the video> | split <project> <clip> <time in its footage | words>
cut.split.help: Cut a clip in two, at a moment of the video or of a clip's footage

cut.transition.help: Change how a clip comes in: the transition (dissolve, fade through black, slide left…) and the sound (start a voice early, let it carry over, or change in a pause)

cut.trim.help: Change where a clip starts or ends in its footage (the rest of the cut moves up), or move a cut

cut.update.usage: metarush cut update <project> [--resources a,b] [--cuts clip,…] [--only resources|cuts]
cut.update.help: Update the latest cut's resources and nested cuts to their newest versions (an explicit change: shown first, then saved)

cut.useFixed.help: Save a new version of the cut that plays a source's fixed copy (or its original again with --original); saved versions never change

cut.where.help: List the cuts that play this project's cut inside them

database.abandon.help: Abandon a move of the database that stopped: changes go on in the old database; the copy keeps its lock (owners, a person at a terminal)

database.move.help: Move the workspace's database to another one: changes pause on every computer, everything is copied and checked, this computer switches; the old database is kept (owners, a person at a terminal)

database.move.status.help: Say whether the workspace is being moved to another database or moved (then switch this computer too), and how the last move here went

database.plan.help: Say what moving the workspace's database would do — what moves, how long it takes, what each computer needs — and check the new database; nothing is changed (owners)

database.switch.help: Switch this computer to the database the workspace moved to, with this computer's own sign-in (owners, a person at this computer)

deliver.captions.usage: metarush deliver captions <delivered video, its .json file, or the folder>
deliver.captions.help: Update the captions files of delivered videos with the text fixes made since (no new render)

deliver.export.help: Export finished videos to a folder on this machine (checked copies with a notes file each; never overwrites, never uploads)

delivery.gate.help: Whether versions wait for the quality check and their sign-offs before they go out; owners turn it on or off (off: people only)

delivery.gate.set.help: Whether versions wait for the quality check and their sign-offs before they go out; owners turn it on or off (off: people only)

delivery.notes.help: Show a version's delivery notes as delivery writes them

delivery.notes.set.help: Save a version's delivery notes (the version itself never changes); typing it yourself, --by claude when you paste what Claude Code wrote

delivery.override.usage: metarush deliver override <project> [--version rN] --note "<why it goes out anyway>"
delivery.override.help: Send a version out anyway past what holds it, with a note (people only: in their own terminal or on the version's page; the note shows on the receipt)

delivery.ready.help: Whether a version can go out to a client: Ready to deliver, or what holds it and how to clear each (--json for every detail)

draft.decide.help: Approve an AI app's draft (people only): a version goes into the cut, a change is made as you

draft.list.help: Drafts AI apps proposed, newest first, with what a person decided (an app sees its own unless it asks for all)

draft.save.help: Propose a change without making it: a new version (a cut sheet, an edit plan, a cut verb) kept beside the cut, or another change kept until a person approves it

edit.apply.help: Save a checked change as a new version (earlier versions stay as they are)

edit.check.help: Check a change before saving it: its problems, what it changes, and whether it is ready to save

edit.preview.help: Try a change without saving it: what it does to the cut and its problems, in plain words

edit.templates.help: List the ready-made graphics (titles, name titles, quotes, end cards, slides) and how long each can be

edit.transitions.help: List the transitions (picture and sound), with when to use each, their lengths, directions and the project styles

export.timeline.help: Write a version of a cut as a timeline for DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro or Premiere Pro

recipe.runs.help: List runs of recipes (when, who, where, cost, approved), or show one with its steps and what it waits for; --wait follows it here

recipe.show.help: Show a recipe: its inputs (type, default, limits), sections, sound, rules, hints, versions, check and runs

recording.list.help: The screen recordings, newest first: their tracks, length and whether they are footage yet

recording.show.help: A screen recording's tracks, where each starts on its clock, its footage and its projects

remotion.words.help: A Remotion source's on-screen words: its settings (as written in the code and as changed), or where its words are written when they aren't settings yet

remotion.words.set.help: Change on-screen words of a Remotion source whose words are settings: drawn with no network and checked (length, words that don't fit), then the cuts' clips are made again — no new version of its code

remotion.words.setup.help: Make a Remotion source's on-screen words settings: one change to its code (its copy files read their words from settings), checked as its next version for a person to approve

render.fetch.help: Save a finished render as a video file (checked against the original)

render.follow.set.help: Whether a review copy follows each cut's latest version (made by itself about a minute after the last change); on or off changes it

render.follow.show.help: Whether a review copy follows each cut's latest version (made by itself about a minute after the last change); on or off changes it

render.submit.help: Render a version (with --wait, wait until the video is ready)

resources.add.usage: metarush resources add <file | folder | GitHub repository | web page>... [--project <project> | --workspace]
resources.add.help: Add pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP; HEIC becomes JPEG), SVGs (cleaned of scripts and outside links), PDFs (pages become pictures) and fonts; a folder is linked and kept in step; a GitHub repository is pinned at a commit; a web page becomes a dated snapshot

resources.fetch.usage: metarush resources add <file | folder | GitHub repository | web page>... [--project <project> | --workspace]
resources.fetch.help: Add pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP; HEIC becomes JPEG), SVGs (cleaned of scripts and outside links), PDFs (pages become pictures) and fonts; a folder is linked and kept in step; a GitHub repository is pinned at a commit; a web page becomes a dated snapshot

resources.folder.usage: metarush resources folder <folder name | id> [--upload …] [--small-mb N] [--pause | --resume] [--path <folder here>] [--rescan]
resources.folder.help: Change a linked folder: when files upload, pause or resume it here, say where it is on this machine, or look through it again

resources.folders.help: List linked folders and how they stand on each machine

resources.link.help: Link a folder on this machine: its pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts become resources (and footage becomes sources), kept in step as files change

resources.list.help: List the resources a project can use (its own, the workspace library's, its linked projects'), or the workspace library

resources.make.usage: metarush resources make <code | diagram | stats> [<repository>] [--file <path> --lines 40-72] [--from <diagram file>]
resources.make.help: Make a code slide (a repository file's lines, highlighted), a diagram (Mermaid or D2, drawn as SVG) or a repository card, as a resource that says where it came from

resources.path.usage: metarush resources path <name | title | id> [--project <project>] [--page N] [--version <sha>]
resources.path.help: Fetch a resource's file (or a PDF page picture) to this machine and print where it is

resources.pictures.help: The pictures a GitHub repository keeps from its folders: each PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG file a picture of its own, pinned to the commit and refreshed with it; --keep and --drop change the folders

resources.pictures.set.help: The pictures a GitHub repository keeps from its folders: each PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG file a picture of its own, pinned to the commit and refreshed with it; --keep and --drop change the folders

resources.promote.help: Move a project's resource into the workspace library, so every project can use it

resources.refresh.help: Look at a resource again (size, colours, PDF page pictures, suggested tags; the file never changes); a repository moves to its newest commit and a web page gets a new snapshot, as new versions cuts use after cut update

resources.remove.help: Remove a resource from the library (nothing is deleted: cuts that use it keep showing it), or bring it back

resources.show.help: Show a resource: versions, size, colours, tags, where it came from and where it is used

resources.unlink.help: Stop keeping a linked folder in step (everywhere, or only on this machine); its resources stay

resources.update.help: Rename a resource, change its short name, tags, description or licence note

resources.where.help: List where a resource is used: cuts (and their older versions) and the brand kit

review.packet.help: One page for a draft or version, to hand to a client or colleague: what changed and why, the checks, the cost, who made it and what is still waiting

review.waiting.help: Awaiting your review: each cut's latest version an AI app (Claude, Codex, Cursor…) made or someone asked to have reviewed, and the drafts AI apps proposed

revision.approve.help: Approve a version (people only: in their own terminal or the dashboard)

revision.askReview.help: Ask for review: the version waits in “Awaiting your review” until someone approves it or says what should change

revision.compare.help: Compare two versions (--format md: the changes in plain words plus the cut sheet lines that differ)

revision.list.help: List a project's versions (* marks the latest)

revision.note.help: Change a version's note: a few words saying what it changed (the version itself never changes); an empty note removes it

revision.plan.help: Show the frame-by-frame plan a render of a version follows (--details or --json for all of it)

revision.show.help: Show a version: what was asked, its clips, warnings and renders (--json has the whole cut)

search.help: Search what was said (transcripts with timecodes), what's on screen (things, places, on-screen text), video titles, projects, versions, comments and resources

setup.status.help: Say what works on this computer: free with no keys, what a key adds, Claude Code and the database

share.create.help: Make a review link to send (a person's step: typed in a terminal, or Share for review… on the version's page)

share.link.help: The link to send again, for a review link that still works (a person's step)

share.list.help: Review links that work now (--all: every one sent), with what each shows and the comments that came back

share.plan.help: What a review link would show, for how long, and whether it may be made (nothing is made)

share.revoke.help: Take a review link back: its page and video are deleted at once, its comment slots once their last comments are read; comments already in stay (a person's step)

share.settings.help: Who may send review links and for how long, and whether this workspace's media store can hold their pages

share.settings.set.help: Turn review links on or off, let only owners send them, or shorten the longest a link lasts (owners, a person's step)

share.sync.help: Bring in new comments from review links now, and end links whose time is up (the dashboard's computer does it every two minutes)

sound.compare.help: How much clearer the voices are: the voice clarity score and the background, before and after, with warnings when it went too far

sound.enhance.help: Make a voice clearer: one person over their speech, the narration, a recording or everyone (the recordings are kept)

sound.levels.help: Change how loud things are: a part (camera sound, narration, music, effects), one person over their speech, a music track, and the automatic help

sound.music.add.help: Put music under the cut: a file on this computer or audio already in the workspace (its title or ID)

sound.music.set.help: Change a music track: fit it to the video or time it by hand, its level, getting quieter when someone talks, looping, or take it out

sound.preview.help: Change how loud things are: a part (camera sound, narration, music, effects), one person over their speech, a music track, and the automatic help

sound.setup.help: Set up clearer voices on this computer: clean (about 30 MB, also set up on first use) or studio (about 1.8 GB) — people only

sound.show.help: The sound in plain words: levels, each person, clearer voices, automatic help and music

storage.migrate.help: Move the footage to another storage (a cloud bucket, Google Cloud Storage or a folder): checked, can be resumed, nothing deleted

storage.plan.help: Move the footage to another storage (a cloud bucket, Google Cloud Storage or a folder): checked, can be resumed, nothing deleted

storage.status.help: Say which storage this computer uses, and whether the workspace moved to another one (then switch this computer too)

sync.status.help: What this machine has a copy of, imports still uploading, jobs, which machines run MetaRush, and whether the database and storage answer

timeline.import.help: Make a new cut from a timeline another editing app exported (OpenTimelineIO, FCPXML, Final Cut Pro 7 XML, EDL), matched to your footage

timeline.read.help: Make a new cut from a timeline another editing app exported (OpenTimelineIO, FCPXML, Final Cut Pro 7 XML, EDL), matched to your footage

todos.acceptShown.help: Use the names a clip shows (a call app's name under each picture, a lower third) for the people it asks about

todos.answer.help: Answer a question (it is applied right away: names the voice or the faces, saves the rights…)

todos.counts.help: How many questions are open, per project and video

todos.dismiss.help: Skip a question (it won't be asked again)

todos.groups.help: Who is on screen: one question per person per clip, with how often they are seen and why a name is suggested

todos.notPerson.help: None of the faces asked about as this person are them (every open face question suggesting them, in a project or a clip)

todos.show.help: One question: what to listen to or look at, and how to answer

todos.skipFaces.help: Skip every open question about faces in a clip or a project (those faces aren't asked about again)

todos.sync.help: Re-check what needs asking (and close questions that no longer apply)

transcript.find.help: Find words in transcripts: every place, with the words around it (nothing changes)

transcript.fix.help: Retype what is said in a stretch: only the words that differ change, each keeping its time; it can be undone

transcript.history.help: A clip's transcript fixes, newest first: who changed what and when, and what can still be undone

transcript.pending.help: Text fixes waiting for a new version of a cut (list), and making that version with one review copy (apply)

transcript.pending.apply.help: Make one new version of the cut with every text fix waiting, and one review copy (nothing renders after each fix)

transcript.replace.help: Change words wherever they are said (or only --only places); joined or split words keep their timing, and it can be undone

transcript.speaker.help: Say who really says a stretch ("this part is Lena, not Maya"); it goes in the clip's transcript history and can be undone

transcript.spelling.add.help: Put a word on the spelling list of a project's own settings (without --project, the default's)

transcript.spelling.apply.help: Correct existing transcripts by the spelling lists (--settings-of: every clip using that project's settings; --dry-run lists the places)

transcript.spelling.list.help: The spelling list a project uses (without --project, the default's)

transcript.spelling.remove.help: Take a word off a spelling list

transcript.spelling.suggestions.help: Words you keep fixing the same way that aren't on a spelling list yet

transcript.undo.help: Undo a transcript fix, a whole find and replace (--batch), or a clip's latest fix (--last)

trash.configure.help: Whether the Trash empties itself after a number of days (off unless a person turns it on)

trash.empty.help: Delete what is in the Trash for good (or only the clips named), with previews, transcripts and speaker data, on every machine; clips a cut uses stay — people only, in their own terminal

trash.list.help: List what is in the Trash: from where, how big, and whether each can be deleted for good

trash.settings.help: Whether the Trash empties itself after a number of days (off unless a person turns it on)

users.disable.help: Turn a person's account off: signed out everywhere, can't sign in (people only)

users.enable.help: Turn a person's account back on (people only)

users.invite.help: Invite a person: a one-time link they follow to choose a password (people only)

users.list.help: The workspace's people, with their roles and whether they can sign in

users.remove.help: Remove a person's account; their name stays on what they did (people only)

users.resetLink.help: A one-time link a person follows to choose a new password (an invite again if they haven't accepted theirs) (people only)

users.revoke.help: Take back a person's invite or reset link (people only)

users.role.help: Make a person an owner or a member (people only)

version.show.help: Print the version (--details: what's new in it, and the version each of your computers runs)

voiceover.addTake.help: Record narration: live while the video plays (--live --from), or line by line with an on-screen prompter

voiceover.align.help: Import a narration recording: store it, transcribe it, match it to the script and place it

voiceover.askFit.help: Fit the script to the video with Claude: lines tied to the right moments, trimmed to fit, every change explained; your original is kept

voiceover.choose.help: Play another take on a line, or switch between the original and cleaned-up version

voiceover.cleanup.help: Clean up recorded narration (noise, rumble, harsh s, uneven level) — the original is kept for A/B

voiceover.clone.help: Make an ElevenLabs voice from recordings of your own voice (people only; anyone else needs their recorded consent)

voiceover.estimate.help: What ElevenLabs narration would cost (characters, credits, budget) — nothing is generated

voiceover.fit.help: Check that every line fits before the next one; --apply builds the fix (it is saved only when you confirm it)

voiceover.fitted.help: Fit the script to the video with Claude: lines tied to the right moments, trimmed to fit, every change explained; your original is kept

voiceover.line.help: Add, change, move or remove one narration line

voiceover.models.help: ElevenLabs models this account can use: languages, longest line, cost per character

voiceover.parse.help: Read a plain-text script: paragraphs become lines; [@shot+0.5] [0:12.4] [after] (notes) place them

voiceover.place.help: Put a live take where it was spoken (or each line at its planned spot); a recording needs --from, where on the video it started

voiceover.preview.help: List voices to choose from (ElevenLabs, its public library, or free local voices); --preview saves a sample

voiceover.scratch.help: Make free scratch narration with a system voice, to check timing before paying for a voice or recording

voiceover.show.help: Each line, where it plays, whether it fits, and its audio

voiceover.takes.help: List the takes for each line, and choose which one plays

voiceover.tts.help: Generate narration with ElevenLabs (unchanged lines are reused for free; --estimate shows the cost first)

voiceover.use.help: Use your original script, or Claude's version fitted to the video (the other is kept with its sound and places)

voiceover.voices.help: List voices to choose from (ElevenLabs, its public library, or free local voices); --preview saves a sample

watch.browse.help: List folders under your home folder (what the dashboard's folder picker shows)

watch.choose.help: Pick the folder with the macOS folder picker (on this machine's screen)

watch.import.help: Also add the files that were already in the folder (when it was set to take only new files)

watch.mkdir.help: Create a folder under your home folder

watch.reveal.help: Open the watched folder in Finder

watch.set.help: Watch a folder: files dropped into it are added automatically (applies without restarting MetaRush)

watch.status.help: Show the watched folder's setup and what it is doing

worker.configure.help: Change the battery level below which big jobs wait for the charger (0 = never wait; people only)

worker.list.help: The machines that do background work, with their battery and when big jobs wait

worker.settings.help: This machine's battery, and the level below which big jobs wait for the charger

workspace.adopt.help: Say this restored copy is now the workspace, so it deletes by itself again as set (owners, people only)

workspace.export.usage: metarush workspace export --to <folder or file> [--media referenced|included] [--tar] [--plan]
workspace.export.help: Export the whole workspace into one archive for a backup or a move (owners, people only; --plan first)

workspace.exports.help: List the exports of the workspace made on this computer and how far each one is (owners, people only)

workspace.show.help: Show the workspace this machine is in
